I am pre-build planning three Jira stories and need the exact current state of the codebase surface they touch:
- SFCC-236 "Product Card Shared Component" — one shared product card with variations for Homepage / PLP / Wishlist / Recently-Viewed-Full-History, driven by a style prop.
- SFCC-83 "Recently Viewed UI Component (Shared)" — horizontal rail of recently-viewed product tiles on PLP, PDP, Cart.
- SFCC-84 "Recently Viewed - See Full History" — a full page listing all recently viewed items.

Report on ALL of the following. Quote real file paths and line numbers. If something does NOT exist, say so explicitly — absence is as important as presence.

1. PRODUCT TILE / CARD, current state:
   - Everything under `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` — full contents, exports (default vs named, e.g. `CardBaseline`), props surface, what it renders.
   - The base version at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-tile/` — what the override changed vs base.
   - Any other card-like component: `ui-kits/**` (atoms/molecules/organisms), `product-item/`, anything named *card*, *tile*.
   - Its Storybook story and any test file.

2. RECENTLY VIEWED — does ANY implementation exist?
   - grep for: recently.viewed, recentlyViewed, RecentlyViewed, recently-viewed, viewedProducts, browsingHistory, recentlyViewedProducts — across `overrides/`, `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`, and `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/`.
   - Is there an SFCC/commerce-sdk hook or API for recently-viewed or browsing history? Check `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` too.
   - `recommended-products/` component — what it is, does it already render a horizontal product rail, is it Einstein-backed?
   - Any existing horizontal-scroll / carousel / rail component anywhere (ProductScroller, Carousel, Swiper, scroller).

3. UI-KITS STRUCTURE (the target pattern):
   - Full tree of `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` — every atom, molecule, organism that exists today, with the file set in each (index.tsx, *.css.ts, *.stories.tsx, *.test.tsx).
   - Read ONE complete exemplar molecule end-to-end (prefer zimmColourSwatchGroup if present, else the most recently added) and describe the four-file pattern precisely: naming, export style, how the recipe is registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`, how `useMultiStyleConfig` is keyed.
   - The current contents of `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (list registered recipe keys).

4. ROUTING (for SFCC-84's new page):
   - `overrides/app/routes.tsx` — full structure, how a route + lazy-loaded page is registered, existing page examples under `overrides/app/pages/`.
   - Is there an existing account/wishlist page pattern to copy?

5. PAGES that would consume these:
   - `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`, any PLP page, `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`, cart page — do they exist as overrides or only in base? Which currently render product tiles, and how?

6. TIER CLASSIFICATION — read `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` and tell me the tier + owner for every path you named above. Do NOT use `.claude/registry/*.md`.

7. BLAST RADIUS — for `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` and any shared component you'd touch: who imports it? Count and list importers in BOTH `overrides/` and `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`.

8. CODEOWNERS — read `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/CODEOWNERS` and report the owning team(s) for each path above.

Be concrete and exhaustive. I need to plan a real build off this, so guessing is worse than saying "not found".

=== frozenFiles.md ===
# Tier 1 — Frozen Files

These files must not be modified by Claude Code without the developer explicitly naming the file
in the prompt AND confirming they have spoken to the listed owner. No exceptions.

> **Note:** this is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 — paths
> below reference `overrides/app/...` (the customisation surface) rather than the upstream
> monorepo `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...` path.

## Design System (Owner: UI Designer — #design-system)

The whole `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` folder is Tier 1. Currently present:

```text
overrides/app/theme/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/motion.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts
```

**Fonts are self-hosted and served on every tier.** `overrides/app/static/fonts/` holds two
Futura Round faces — Regular 400 and Medium 500 — declared by
`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` and mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and
`.storybook/preview.tsx`. Only two faces exist because only two are used: all 22 textStyles
resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.

There is **no environment gate** on this, and it is worth stating plainly because an earlier
revision of this section claimed there was. `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally inside
`_app-config`'s `ChakraProvider`, and `pwa-kit-dev`'s `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies
`overrides/app/static` in both the client and SSR webpack configs — so the `.woff2` are
published with every bundle and shoppers on every storefront render Futura Round.

`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
design-parity review against Figma.

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` (**Tier 2**) or, per
the co-location pattern, beside their component as `<name>.css.ts` — governed by that
component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead, not this Tier — see
[protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`
variables defined in `foundation/zimmTokens.ts`, so it is derived styling rather than a
brand token source, but it emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner.

## Commerce SDK Hooks (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-token.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.ts
```

Note: `commerce-sdk-react` is consumed from `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/` —
it is not in this repo and cannot be modified here. The hooks above are the overrides surface.

## Runtime & Integration Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
config/                              ← entire directory (default.js, sites.js, sit.js, dev.js, utils.js)
overrides/app/ssr.js
overrides/app/ssr/                   ← SSR helper modules split from ssr.js in refactor 610020e:
                                         connectionPools.ts  — undici pool isolation (blast-radius mitigation)
                                         contentSecurityPolicy.ts  — CSP headers; wrong change = security hole on every page
                                         slasTokens.ts  — SLAS auth token handling; wrong change = broken auth site-wide
                                         paymentMetadata.ts  — payment method metadata SSR (checkout pages)
                                         marketingCloud.ts  — MC client-credentials token exchange
worker/main.js
package.json (root)
mobify.config.js
overrides/app/config/countries.ts
overrides/app/config/contentful.ts   ← gates preview/draft content; removing the server-side check exposes drafts on production
```

**`overrides/app/request-processor.js` — add here when populated.**
Currently the Salesforce example stub. Once Zimmermann's geo-redirect and storefront-routing logic lands here it runs on every single request — it will be one of the highest-blast-radius files in the repo. Add it to this section before that work begins.

## Build Pipeline (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

Path aliases are configured in four places that must stay in sync (see architecture.md §Path Aliases).
Breaking either file silently breaks every `app/` and `~` import across the codebase.

```text
babel.config.js    ← path aliases for npm start dev server + production build
tsconfig.json      ← path aliases for TypeScript / VS Code intellisense; also enforces strict mode
```

## Consent (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
Didomi / consent configuration (paths TBD — add when introduced)
```

## Test & Tooling Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

Mirrors AGENTS.md hard rule 8 — test config drift breaks every contributor's harness.

```text
vitest.config.*
vitest.setup.ts       ← test environment setup; complements vitest.config.*
playwright.config.*
.storybook/
lighthouserc.js
browserstack.yml      ← must target e2e/tests/zimm only; scope change = CI cost explosion + upstream test failures.
                         Named without a leading dot deliberately — browserstack-node-sdk requires exactly this
                         filename (renamed from .browserstack.yml on 2026-08-25 — SFCC-751; the old dotfile name
                         made every SDK-driven run fail at config resolution before any test executed).
```

## CI/CD Pipeline (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
.github/workflows/
```

## Governance (Owner: Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead — #dev-team)

```text
AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md
CODEOWNERS
.claude/rules/
.claude/settings.json
coderabbit.yaml              ← AI PR review config; weakening it removes Tier 1 change detection and commit-format enforcement
.coderabbit/                 ← ast-grep rule content coderabbit.yaml points at; weakening/deleting a rule here silently removes that check with no signal in coderabbit.yaml itself
semgrep.yml                  ← semgrep rule content (payment-credential-logging, XSS); same silent-weakening risk as .coderabbit/
scripts/hooks/pre-commit     ← enforces Contentful drift check and blocks direct edits to derived AI config files
scripts/hooks/commit-msg     ← enforces conventional commits; /generate-changelog depends on this
```

############################
=== protectedFiles.md ===
# Tier 2 — Protected Files

These can be modified on a feature branch but require a PR review from a developer who is not
the author before merging to develop.

> Paths reference `overrides/app/...` per this project's slim overrides layout. Override files
> keep the original Salesforce filename (kebab-case) but are TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`).

## Global Shell (Owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching)

```text
overrides/app/components/header/
overrides/app/components/footer/
overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/
overrides/app/components/list-menu/
overrides/app/components/seo/
overrides/app/components/_app/
overrides/app/components/_app-config/
overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/
overrides/app/routes.tsx
```

`uiCopyProvider/` is mounted once inside `_app-config` and provides `useUiCopy()`'s context
value to every page on every site — the same blast radius as `_app-config` itself, so it
belongs in this tier alongside it rather than defaulting to Tier 4 by omission.

## Shared Product Components (Owner: Squad B — notify Squad A)

```text
overrides/app/components/product-tile/
overrides/app/components/product-item/
overrides/app/components/display-price/
overrides/app/components/image-gallery/
overrides/app/components/swatch-group/
overrides/app/components/recommended-products/
```

## Shared Commerce Components (Owner: Squad A — notify Squad B)

```text
overrides/app/components/order-summary/
overrides/app/components/promo-code/
overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/
```

## Theme Component Styles (Owner: UI Designer — notify before changing)

```text
overrides/app/theme/components/
overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts
```

One file per Chakra component (e.g. `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`). Register new
files in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`. Foundations live alongside
in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` and are **Tier 1** — see
[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md).

A component's own recipe may instead live beside it as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g.
`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`) rather than here — see
[overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md)'s co-location pattern, introduced with the
footer decomposition. It's still registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`
either way. A co-located `<name>.css.ts` is **not** governed by this section's Tier 2
UI-designer gate — CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule routes it to
the owning squad(s) only. This folder's Tier 2 designation still applies to whatever
hasn't moved to co-location, and to genuinely cross-component shared values (e.g.
`footerShared.ts`) that a single component's file can't own.

`globalStyles.ts` is the `.zimm-*` global class registry, composed into
`theme/index.ts` as `styles.global`. It is derived from the `--zimm-*` variables in
`foundation/zimmTokens.ts` rather than defining brand values itself, so it sits at
Tier 2 — but it emits CSS on every page, so treat a change here as wider-reaching
than a single component override.

## Translations (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — notify before changing)

```text
translations/
overrides/app/static/translations/
```

## Shared Hooks — 5+ consumers (Owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching)

```text
overrides/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-modal-state.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-currency.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-dnt-notification.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-app-origin.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-selected-store.ts
```

## Environment Switching Tooling (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — notify before changing)
`scripts/switchEnv.mjs` (`npm run env`) manages `.env.shared`/`.env.<tier>` locally and gates
`push` — writing shared/tier values to this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per
deployment tier under Settings > Environments) — to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. The
script's own gh-identity check is a fast-fail convenience only, same reasoning as
[AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval](../../AGENTS.md#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) section
— the real enforcement is GitHub itself: writing an Environment Variable requires repo Admin,
which only tier-1-approvers hold. A careless change here could weaken that gate, or misroute a
personal credential (Jira/Confluence token, Contentful CMA token) into the centrally-shared
store instead of keeping it local-only — see the `scope:personal` handling documented in
`.env.sample`'s header before changing the scope-parsing logic.
```text
scripts/switchEnv.mjs
```

## Contentful Schema Definitions (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — notify before changing)

These files define the Zimmermann content model, authored once as a single
organization-scoped Contentful **Environment Template** (`npm run sync:contentful`,
via `client.environmentTemplate.*` in the `contentful-management` SDK) and installed
into each environment (`npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>`). This replaced
an earlier per-environment `sync.js` + migration-file pipeline once Contentful moved to
recommending organization-level content models over independently-synced
space/environment content types.

`content-types/*.js` is the sole source of truth per content type (including
`localized`/`required`/`validations` — there is no longer a separate migration file that
overrides an inferior default). Field deletion during an install is opt-in
(`--delete-deleted-fields`), off by default — a mistaken field definition pushed to the
production Contentful environment is difficult to undo and may break running components.

```text
scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js
scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs
scripts/contentful/content-types/
```

Always run `install:contentful` against a non-production Contentful environment first.
Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` and `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` (local / CI only —
never deployed to MRT).

29	/**
30	 * A component for fetching and rendering product recommendations from the Einstein API
31	 * by a zone or a recommender name.
32	 */
33	const RecommendedProducts = ({zone, recommender, products, title, shouldFetch, ...props}) => {
34	    const {
35	        isLoading,
36	        recommendations,
37	        getZoneRecommendations,
38	        getRecommendations,
39	        sendClickReco,
40	        sendViewReco
41	    } = useEinstein()
42	    const {data: customer} = useCurrentCustomer()
43	    const {customerId} = customer
44	    const {data: wishlist} = useWishList()
45	    const dataCloud = useDataCloud()
46	
47	    const createCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation(
48	        'createCustomerProductListItem'
49	    )
50	    const deleteCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation(
51	        'deleteCustomerProductListItem'
52	    )
53	    const toast = useToast()
54	    const navigate = useNavigation()
55	    const {formatMessage} = useIntl()
56	
57	    const ref = useRef()
58	    const isOnScreen = useIntersectionObserver(ref, {useOnce: true})
59	    const [_products, setProducts] = useState(products)
60	
61	    useEffect(() => {
62	        // Check if the component should fetch results or not. This is useful
63	        // when you are still waiting on additional data, like `products`.
64	        if (typeof shouldFetch === 'function' && !shouldFetch()) {
65	            return
66	        }
67	
68	        // Fetch either zone or recommender, but not both. If a zone and recommender
69	        // name are both provided, `zone` takes precendence.
70	        if (zone) {
71	            getZoneRecommendations(zone, _products)
72	            return
73	        }
74	        if (recommender) {
75	            getRecommendations(recommender, _products)
76	            return
77	        }
78	    }, [zone, recommender, _products])
79	
80	    useEffect(() => {
81	        // This is an optimization that eliminates superfluous rerenders/fetching by
82	        // keeping a copy of the `products` array prop in state for shallow comparison.
83	        if (!Array.isArray(products)) {
84	            return
85	        }
86	        if (
87	            products.length !== _products?.length ||
88	            !products.every((val, index) => val === _products?.[index])
89	        ) {
90	            setProducts(products)
91	        }
92	    }, [products])
93	
94	    useEffect(() => {
95	        if (isOnScreen && recommendations?.recs) {
96	            sendViewReco(
97	                {
98	                    recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
99	                    __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID
100	                },
101	                recommendations.recs.map((rec) => ({id: rec.id}))
102	            )

104	                {
105	                    recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
106	                    __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID
107	                },
108	                recommendations.recs.map((rec) => ({id: rec.id}))
109	            )
110	        }
111	    }, [isOnScreen, recommendations])
112	
113	    // The component should remove itself altogether if it has no recommendations
114	    // and we aren't loading any.
115	    if (!isLoading && (!recommendations || recommendations.length < 1)) {
116	        return null
117	    }
118	
119	    // TODO: DRY this handler when intl provider is available globally
120	    const addItemToWishlist = async (product) => {
121	        try {
122	            if (!wishlist || !customerId) {
123	                return
124	            }
125	            await createCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync({
126	                parameters: {
127	                    listId: wishlist.id,
128	                    customerId
129	                },
130	                body: {
131	                    quantity: 1,
132	                    productId: product.productId,
133	                    public: false,
134	                    priority: 1,
135	                    type: 'product'
136	                }
137	            })
138	
139	            toast({
140	                title: formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST, {quantity: 1}),
141	                status: 'success',
142	                action: (
143	                    // it would be better if we could use <Button as={Link}>
144	                    // but unfortunately the Link component is not compatible
145	                    // with Chakra Toast, since the ToastManager is rendered via portal
146	                    // and the toast doesn't have access to intl provider, which is a
147	                    // requirement of the Link component.
148	                    <Button variant="link" onClick={() => navigate('/account/wishlist')}>
149	                        {formatMessage(TOAST_ACTION_VIEW_WISHLIST)}
150	                    </Button>
151	                )
152	            })
153	        } catch {
154	            toast({
155	                title: formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE),
156	                status: 'error'
157	            })
158	        }
159	    }
160	
161	    const removeItemFromWishlist = async (product) => {
162	        try {
163	            const wishlistItem = wishlist?.customerProductListItems?.find(
164	                (item) => item.productId === product.productId
165	            )
166	            if (!wishlistItem || !wishlist || !customerId) {
167	                return
168	            }
169	            await deleteCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync({
170	                parameters: {
171	                    customerId,
172	                    itemId: wishlistItem.id,
173	                    listId: wishlist.id
174	                }
175	            })
176	            toast({
177	                title: formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_REMOVED_FROM_WISHLIST),
178	                status: 'success',
179	                id: product.productId
180	            })
181	        } catch {
182	            toast({
183	                title: formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE),
184	                status: 'error'
185	            })
186	        }
187	    }
188	
189	    return (
190	        <ProductScroller
191	            ref={ref}
192	            title={title || recommendations?.displayMessage}
193	            products={recommendations.recs}
194	            isLoading={isLoading}
195	            productTileProps={(product) => ({
196	                onClick: () => {
197	                    sendClickReco(
198	                        {
199	                            recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
200	                            __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID
201	                        },
202	                        product
203	                    )

213	            })}
214	            {...props}
215	        />
216	    )
217	}

=== overrideStyling.md lines 90-210 ===

Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
there's no interactive state to lose.

## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component

If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import, which is correct for that file).

The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
override and isn't.

**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.

An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.

## Component-local tokens

When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
— `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
`marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.

See `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` and
`.../footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` for the pattern in a real recipe. The reason is
traceability, not parity with the base theme: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference names the
Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these
recipes are deliberately namespaced `ZimmFooter*` so they do **not** inherit the base
SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)

**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

The array shorthand (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`) is what this section used to
recommend, and it would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks
responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail.
`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.

When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
`header.ts`/`zimmButton.css.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.

If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put
Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default and adds

recipe rather than a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't require a second

     3	 * reads off `useMultiStyleConfig`.
     4	 *
     5	 * The failure this catches is silent, though not by the mechanism it looks like: `parts` does

     7	 * `parts: ['declared']` while carrying both parts in `baseStyle` and in a variant resolves to
     8	 * `{declared: {...base, ...variant}, undeclared: {...base}}` — the undeclared part keeps its
     9	 * full base styling and loses only the variant's. `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes`. The base

    11	 * declared `parts` against 13 `baseStyle` keys, and the four it omits (`accountIcon`,

    13	 * `components/header/index.jsx` (lines 232, 255, 321, 323) today.

    16	 * renders correctly and then stops responding to variants and sizes — latent on a recipe with no
    17	 * variants today, surfacing only the day someone adds one. If `baseStyle` does not, the read is
    18	 * `undefined`, `__css={undefined}` is a legal prop, and the element inherits. Neither is reported
    19	 * by `tsc`, eslint, an axe run, or a `play` that only asserts text. The first case is precisely
    20	 * the "would survive a refactor invisibly if broken" case .claude/rules/testing.md says to cover,
    21	 * so the corrected mechanism strengthens this guard's justification rather than weakening it.

    24	 * part in both places at once keeps them consistent with each other and still breaks the

Split out of [conventions.md](./conventions.md) — see that file for cross-cutting 5 rules that apply to every file regardless of type (TypeScript-only, DRY/KISS/SOLID, magic 6 numbers, security). TypeScript idioms live in [typescript.md](./typescript.md); Chakra/CSS 7 conventions live in [css.md](./css.md). 8 9 --- 10 11 ## Components 12 13 - **Named export** matches the folder name (e.g. `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`). 14 No default exports of anonymous functions. 15 - **Props type name** matches the component name: `ProductTileProps` for `ProductTile`, 16 `TopNavProps` for `TopNav`. 17 - **Props type placement:** 18 - _Default:_ declare the `Props` type at the top of the component file. 19 - _Move to `types.ts` in the same folder_ only when (a) the type is consumed by sibling 20 files (story, test, sub-components) **or** (b) it exceeds ~30 lines and mixes with 21 other shared types worth co-locating. 22 - The trigger is _shared consumption_, not line count alone. 23 - **JSDoc** is required on: 24 25 - Any component used by ≥2 callers (shared components — typically Tier 2 in 26 [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md)). 27 - Any exported hook. 28 - Any utility function with non-obvious behaviour. 29 30 Leaf components used by a single page don't need JSDoc — the prop type is sufficient. 31 32 - **Callback props** follow `onEventName` (e.g. `onAddToCart`, `onClose`). 33 - **Required props are non-optional;** optional props use `?` — no `| undefined` unions 34 for "I forgot to mark it optional." 35 - **Accessibility (JSX) — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`, so get 36 these right at authoring time:** 37 - Every `` needs an `alt` attribute (`alt=""` is fine for purely decorative images). 38 - Every `IconButton` (including wrapped variants like `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs 39 an `aria-label` — it renders no visible text, so screen readers have nothing else to 40 announce. 41 - Any element with an `onClick` that isn't natively interactive (`div`, `span`, `Box`, 42 `Flex`, `Stack`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Grid`, `Text`, and similar) needs a `role` 43 attribute at minimum — and for real keyboard operability, also `tabIndex={0}` and an 44 `onKeyDown` handler (or just use a `Button`/native interactive element instead, which 45 is almost always simpler than reimplementing keyboard behaviour). 46 47 --- 48 49 ## Composition — writing a "clean" component 50 51 Rules of thumb for when a component is doing too much and should be split, or when inline 52 state belongs in a custom hook instead. 53 54 - **Complexity / size.** A component function should stay roughly under ~150 lines and 55 avoid deep branching (rule of thumb: ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity — count independent 56 paths through the render logic, not total lines). **This is not currently ESLint-enforced** 57 — `.eslintrc.js` has no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule configured today, so 58 treat this as a self-check during authoring and something `/code-quality` should flag, not 59 something the build will fail on yet.
